# `assembly`

```{image} ../_static/pipeline_assembly.svg
:width: 100%
:class: no-scaled-link
:align: center
```

The `assembly` module takes a sample list CSV file paired with cleaned, decontaminated paired-end FASTQ files—typically generated by the preprocessing step—and assembles them into contigs. By default, assembly is performed using `MEGAHIT`, though users can explicitly specify the assembler via the `assembler` to the `MEGAHIT` option. To accommodate diverse experimental setups, co-assembly can be enabled by assigning identical identifiers to multiple sample IDs in the "assembly" column of the sample list file. Support for alternative assemblers, such as `metaSPAdes`, is also under active development, though co-assembly features may vary by tool. The module ultimately outputs a FASTA contig file for each sample alongside a comprehensive contig summary report detailing the size and distribution of the assembled contigs.

## Quick Run

::::{tab-set}
:::{tab-item} Sample List

**`Conda`**

```bash
snakemake --sdm conda --use-conda --config module="assembly" assembler="megahit" outdir="sample/results" datadir="sample/fastq" samplelist="sample/sample_list.csv" -j 16 --latency-wait 20
```

**`Apptainer`**

```bash
snakemake --sdm conda apptainer --config module="assembly" assembler="megahit" outdir="sample/results" datadir="sample/fastq" samplelist="sample/sample_list.csv" -j 16 --latency-wait 20
```

**`HPC (PBS) (Conda)`**

```bash
EMAIL="youremail@protonmail.com"
snakemake --sdm conda --use-conda --config module="assembly" assembler="megahit" outdir="sample/results" datadir="sample/fastq" samplelist="sample/sample_list.csv" -j 88 --latency-wait 20 --executor cluster-generic --cluster-generic-submit-cmd "qsub -N {log} -l nodes=1:ppn={threads} -l mem={resources.mem_mb}m -l walltime=120:00:00 -M $EMAIL -q cgsd -o qsub.log -e qsub.log -m a"
```

**`HPC (PBS) (Apptainer)`**

```bash
EMAIL="youremail@protonmail.com"
snakemake --sdm conda apptainer --config module="assembly" assembler="megahit" outdir="sample/results" datadir="sample/fastq" samplelist="sample/sample_list.csv" -j 88 --latency-wait 20 --executor cluster-generic --cluster-generic-submit-cmd "qsub -N {log} -l nodes=1:ppn={threads} -l mem={resources.mem_mb}m -l walltime=120:00:00 -M $EMAIL -q cgsd -o qsub.log -e qsub.log -m a"
```

:::
::::

``` {admonition} Dry Run
:class: Tip
Use the `-n` flag with your command to perform a dry-run first, listing all analyses that will be performed 
```

## Configuration

- **`assembler`:** The primary assembly tool engine selected for the assembly module (spades support is currently in development). (default: "megahit")
- **`megahit-min-len`:** The minimum contig length threshold used during the MEGAHIT assembly filter steps. (default: 300)
- **`megahit-params`:** Additional runtime parameters supplied directly to the MEGAHIT execution pipeline. (default: "--prune-level 3")
- **`spades-params`:** Additional runtime parameters supplied directly to the SPAdes metagenomic assembler execution line. (default: "--meta")
- **`spades-memory`:** The upper threshold of RAM memory (in gigabytes) allocated for SPAdes assembly execution. (default: 250)

## Outputs

```bash
assembly/megahit
├── samples
    ├── SampleA
        ├── output
            ├── checkpoints.txt
            ├── done
            ├── final.contigs.fa
            ├── intermediate_contigs
        ├── log
        ├── options.json
    ├── SampleB
    ├── SampleC
├── logs
├── benchmarks
├── reports
└── tmp
```

The main output from this module is the assembly file `final.contigs.fa` which includes the final contigs generated by `megahit` or `SPAdes`. These contigs will be used for many steps in downstream analysis.
